content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I've reviewed the development process I'll be following. We're at the very start of the first cycle — **Phase 1, Goal exploration** — so before anything technical, I'd like to understand what you're really after.

Let me start with the *why*:

**When this bookmark app is finished and you're using it, what would be different from how you handle things today?** For example — is there a specific frustration with how you currently save or find things, or something you wish you could do but can't right now?

And a related one: **when you picture yourself reaching for this app, what's the moment?** Are you saving something you just found and want to get back to later, or is it more about coming back to a big pile of saved things and trying to find the right one?

Your answers here steer everything that follows, so there are no wrong answers — I'm just trying to picture your world before we shape the tool.

Right now my bookmarks become a big, messy pile, so I often can’t find something when I need it.

I want to quickly save a link I’ve just found, have the app pick up its basic details for me, and optionally add tags or a note. Later, I want to search or filter the collection easily, including keeping “read later” items separate. I’d also like to archive links I want to keep without cluttering the main view.

content:
That's really clear — thank you. Let me play back what I heard to make sure I've got the heart of it right.

**The core problem:** today your bookmarks pile up into one big messy heap, and when you actually need something, you can't find it.

**So the real goal isn't just "storing links" — it's being able to *find the right one later, with confidence.*** The saving is the easy part; the payoff is retrieval and keeping the pile from turning into clutter again.

From what you described, the app would help you:
- **Save a link fast** the moment you find it, and have the app fill in the basic details for you
- **Optionally add your own tags or a note** so it's yours, not just a raw URL
- **Find things again later** by searching or filtering
- **Keep "read later" items in their own lane**, separate from everything else
- **Archive links you want to keep** without them cluttering your main view

**Is that the right direction?** And is there anything I've over- or under-emphasized — for instance, is the "read later" flow something you lean on heavily, or more of a nice-to-have next to plain searching?

One more thing before we go further: when you imagine using this, **what kind of app do you have in mind — something in a web browser, on your phone, on your desktop, or something else?** That choice shapes how I'll show you working screens as we go.

Yes, that’s the right direction. Finding things again is the main priority; “read later” is useful, but secondary to good search, tags, and filtering.

I picture it primarily as a web app I can use in a browser, with a layout that also works comfortably on my phone.

content:
The search box now understands precise queries. On **http://maker:4001**, try these, one at a time, and watch the list respond:

1. Type `#reference` — only bookmarks carrying that **exact tag** show (3 of them).
2. Type `"chocolate chip"` — the quotes find that **exact phrase**; you get just the cookies recipe.
3. Type `cooking OR testing` — you get **either** — two bookmarks.
4. Type `#reference NOT css` — the reference ones **except** the CSS one.
5. Type `(cooking OR testing) AND #tools` — **parentheses** group the choice; you land on the one testing tool.
6. Try `REFERENCE` in capitals — same results as lowercase; **capitalization is ignored** everywhere.

Choices I made — please react to these:

- **`#tag` matches the whole tag exactly** — `#css` finds the tag `css`, but wouldn't match a tag called `css-tricks`. I assumed a tag filter should be precise. Is exact-match what you'd expect, or would you want `#ref` to catch `reference` too?
- **AND / OR / NOT are treated as commands in any capitalization.** So to search for the actual *word* "and", you'd wrap it in quotes: `"salt and pepper"`. Does that trade-off suit you?
- **The box stays forgiving while you type** — a half-finished query like `(cooking OR` just narrows as far as it can instead of showing an error.

Does this precise-search behaviour match what you had in mind?

Yes, this matches what I had in mind. `#tag` should match the whole tag exactly, and quoting words such as `"and"` when I mean them literally is a reasonable rule. The forgiving behavior for unfinished searches also sounds helpful.

We've now explored the full happy path *and* the edge cases across every feature, and nine flows are settled. Here's the whole picture we've agreed on, in plain terms:

**Saving**
- Paste a link, press **Get details**, and the app fills in the title and description for you to tweak; add optional tags and a note, then save.
- If a link's details can't be fetched, you're told clearly and can still add a title and save — it never blocks you.
- Re-saving a link you already have doesn't create a duplicate — it brings up the existing one to update instead. You can also edit any bookmark anytime.

**Finding**
- One search box searches across everything — title, description, tags, note, and address — live, and ignoring capitalization.
- Multiple words narrow the results; you can also do precise searches with `#tag`, "exact phrases," and `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` / parentheses. Unfinished searches stay forgiving.

**Keeping it tidy**
- **Read later** gives flagged items their own focused view while they stay in your main list; **Mark as read** retires them from that lane.
- **Archive** tucks links out of your main view and normal searches, findable in the Archived view and restorable anytime.
- **Delete** removes a bookmark for good, with an inline "are you sure?" confirmation.
- Every view has a friendly empty state.

Before I switch from *facilitating* to *building*, two scope points to confirm in plain language:

- The app should **remember your bookmarks between visits** (they persist), as **your own private collection with no sign-in** for this first version — is that right?
- Everything above is the scope for this first version; anything new we think of later, I'll note for a future round rather than expanding this build.

**May I start implementing this scope?** Once you say yes, I'll move into development.
Yes, that’s right: bookmarks should persist between visits as my private, single-user collection, with no sign-in for this first version. The agreed scope is sufficient—please start implementing it.

Development and verification are complete. I'm now in **Phase 4 (Acceptance)**.

## Your bookmarks app is ready to use

**Open it here: http://maker:4000**

It starts empty — your own private, single-user collection that **persists between visits**. Paste a real link and it will genuinely fetch that page's title and description for you.

### What I verified

I checked the built software against **every one of the nine behaviours we approved together**, plus internal quality tests — **44 automated checks in total, all passing**:

- **Acceptance tests (19):** drive the real app in a browser and confirm each approved flow behaves as agreed.
- **Unit tests (25):** the search query engine, duplicate-matching rule, page-details parsing, and the saved-data store.

### The approved behaviours, all working in the real app

- **Save** a link with **Get details**; edit the title/description; add optional tags and a note. If details can't be fetched, you're told and can still save.
- **No duplicates** — re-saving a link you already have brings up the existing one to update; you can edit any bookmark anytime.
- **Find** with one search box across everything — plain words (narrowing, case-insensitive) and precise queries: `#tag`, `"exact phrase"`, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/parentheses, staying forgiving while you type.
- **Read later** lane with a flag in your main list and **Mark as read** to retire items.
- **Archive** to declutter (hidden from All and normal searches, searchable in the Archived view, restorable).
- **Delete** permanently, with an inline "are you sure?" confirmation.
- **Friendly empty states** in every view.

The presentation-only items we deferred (mobile polish, very-long-text wrapping, large-collection performance) are recorded for a later round, as agreed.
